questions.prompt: Why was Jan away yesterday?

audioScript.speaker: Jan
audioScript.de: Entschuldigung. Ich hatte einen Arzttermin.
audioScript.en: Sorry. I had a doctor's appointment.

audioScript.speaker: Petra
audioScript.de: Kein Problem. Konntest du die E-Mails noch lesen?

audioScript.speaker: Jan

audioScript.speaker: Petra
audioScript.de: Das musst du nicht erklären. Die Besprechung war sowieso kurz.
audioScript.en: You don't have to explain. The meeting was short anyway.

audioScript.speaker: Jan
audioScript.de: Danke. Ich hatte wirklich keine Zeit.
audioScript.en: Thanks. I really had no time.

audioScript.en: Only on the first day. In the end we had sun every day.

audioScript.speaker: Tom
audioScript.de: Gut. Ich bringe meinen Freund mit. Er hilft dir auch.
audioScript.en: Good. I will bring my friend along. He will help you too.

questions.prompt: Complete: “___ es möglich, den Termin zu verschieben?”

questions.prompt: What does “Ich hätte eine Frage” express?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is NOT correct?

questions.prompt: What does the guest want first?
questions.explanation: The guest asks: Könnte ich morgen etwas später auschecken?

audioScript.speaker: Rezeption
audioScript.de: Guten Abend, Hotel Sonne. Wie kann ich Ihnen helfen?
audioScript.en: Good evening, Hotel Sonne. How can I help you?

audioScript.speaker: Gast
audioScript.de: Guten Abend. Ich wohne in Zimmer 214. Könnte ich morgen etwas später auschecken?
audioScript.en: Good evening. I am staying in room 214. Could I check out a little later tomorrow?

audioScript.speaker: Rezeption
audioScript.de: Bis wann bräuchten Sie das Zimmer denn?
audioScript.en: Until when would you need the room, then?

audioScript.speaker: Gast
audioScript.de: Wäre zwölf Uhr möglich? Mein Zug fährt erst um zwei.
audioScript.en: Would twelve o'clock be possible? My train does not leave until two.

audioScript.speaker: Rezeption
audioScript.de: Zwölf Uhr ist kein Problem. Ich trage es ein. Möchten Sie noch ein Frühstück dazubuchen?
audioScript.en: Twelve o'clock is no problem. I will make a note of it. Would you like to add breakfast?

audioScript.speaker: Gast
audioScript.de: Nein, danke. Aber könnten Sie mir ein Taxi zum Bahnhof bestellen?
audioScript.en: No, thank you. But could you order me a taxi to the station?

audioScript.speaker: Rezeption
audioScript.de: Natürlich. Ich rufe Sie morgen um elf Uhr an, bevor das Taxi kommt.
audioScript.en: Of course. I will call you tomorrow at eleven, before the taxi arrives.

questions.explanation: Hund is the direct object and masculine, so der becomes den.

questions.prompt: Ich kaufe ___ Apfel.
questions.explanation: Apfel is masculine and the direct object, so ein becomes einen.

questions.prompt: Wir besuchen ___ Stadt.
questions.explanation: Stadt is feminine. Feminine articles do not change in the accusative: die Stadt.

questions.prompt: Build: “Do you live in Berlin?”
questions.answer: Wohnst du in Berlin?
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions start with the conjugated verb: Wohnst du …?

questions.prompt: Ich habe ___ Auto.
questions.explanation: Auto is neuter and indefinite, so kein takes the neuter form: kein Auto.

questions.prompt: ___ wohnst du?
questions.explanation: Wo asks about place: Wo wohnst du? = Where do you live?

questions.prompt: Ich helfe ___ Kind.
questions.explanation: helfen takes the dative. Kind is neuter, so the dative article is dem.

questions.prompt: Ich danke ___ Lehrerin.
questions.explanation: danken takes the dative. Lehrerin is feminine, so die becomes der.

questions.prompt: Das Buch gehört ___.
questions.explanation: gehören takes the dative, and the dative pronoun for ich is mir.

questions.prompt: Ich ___ gestern einen Film gesehen.
questions.explanation: sehen takes haben in the Perfekt: ich habe gesehen.

questions.prompt: Wir ___ nach Hause gegangen.
questions.explanation: gehen expresses movement, so the auxiliary is sein: wir sind gegangen.

questions.prompt: Which participle is correct for essen?
questions.explanation: essen is irregular: gegessen.

questions.prompt: Ich ___ heute länger arbeiten.
questions.explanation: müssen has no ending in the ich form: ich muss. The main verb arbeiten goes to the end.

questions.prompt: Build: “I can come tomorrow.”
questions.answer: Ich kann morgen kommen.
questions.explanation: The modal verb is in position two and the infinitive is at the end.

questions.prompt: Er ___ nicht rauchen.
questions.explanation: dürfen expresses permission. The er form has no ending: er darf.

questions.prompt: Build: “I am learning German because I want to study in Germany.”
questions.answer: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
questions.explanation: In a weil-clause the conjugated verb moves to the end: … weil ich … studieren möchte.

questions.prompt: Ich bleibe zu Hause, ___ es regnet.
questions.explanation: weil introduces a reason and sends the verb to the end: weil es regnet.

questions.prompt: Which word order is correct?
questions.explanation: The subordinate clause is verb-final: weil ich keine Zeit habe.

questions.prompt: Das Buch liegt ___ dem Tisch.
questions.explanation: Position with a two-way preposition takes the dative: auf dem Tisch.

questions.prompt: Ich lege das Buch ___ den Tisch.
questions.explanation: legen expresses direction, so auf takes the accusative: auf den Tisch.

questions.prompt: Wir gehen ___ die Schule.
questions.explanation: Direction into a building uses in + accusative: in die Schule.

questions.prompt: Das ist der Kollege, ___ mir geholfen hat.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of the clause, so masculine der stays der.

questions.prompt: Die Frau, ___ ich kenne, ist meine Nachbarin.
questions.explanation: Frau is feminine and the relative pronoun is the direct object, but feminine stays die in the accusative.

questions.prompt: Build: “That is the colleague who helped me.”
questions.answer: Das ist der Kollege, der mir geholfen hat.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun opens the clause and the conjugated verb hat moves to the end.

questions.prompt: Wenn ich Zeit ___, würde ich mitkommen.
questions.explanation: An unreal condition uses Konjunktiv II: wenn ich Zeit hätte.

questions.prompt: ___ Sie mir bitte helfen?
questions.explanation: Könnten is the polite Konjunktiv II form. It makes the request less direct.

questions.prompt: Ich ___ gern nach Berlin fahren.
questions.explanation: würde + infinitive expresses a wish or hypothetical plan: ich würde fahren.

questions.prompt: Die Rechnung ___ morgen bezahlt.
questions.explanation: The present passive is werden + past participle. Rechnung is singular: wird bezahlt.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is passive?
options: Die Rechnung wird vom Kunden bezahlt.
questions.explanation: werden + past participle marks the passive. The agent is introduced with von.

questions.prompt: Die Fenster ___ gestern geöffnet.
questions.explanation: The past passive uses wurde/wurden. Fenster is plural: wurden geöffnet.

questions.prompt: Es regnet, ___ gehe ich spazieren.
questions.explanation: deshalb introduces a consequence and occupies position one, so the verb follows immediately: deshalb gehe ich.

questions.prompt: Ich bleibe zu Hause, ___ ich krank bin.
questions.explanation: weil introduces a reason and sends the conjugated verb to the end.

questions.prompt: Build: “I am tired, but I am going to work.”
questions.answer: Ich bin müde, aber ich gehe zur Arbeit.
questions.explanation: aber is coordinating, so the word order after it stays normal: aber ich gehe …

questions.prompt: Ich habe einen ___ Film gesehen.
questions.explanation: After einen in the accusative masculine, the adjective takes -en: einen neuen Film.

questions.prompt: Das ist eine ___ Wohnung.
questions.explanation: After eine in the nominative feminine, the adjective takes -e: eine neue Wohnung.

questions.prompt: Der ___ Film war gut.
questions.explanation: After the definite article der, the nominative masculine adjective takes the weak ending -e: der neue Film.

questions.prompt: Die Ministerin sagte, die Reform ___ notwendig.
questions.explanation: Reported speech uses Konjunktiv I. The form of sein for die Reform is sei.
questions.sourceLabel: Konjunktiv I & Reported Speech · Grammar drill

questions.prompt: Reported speech typically uses…
questions.explanation: Konjunktiv I signals that the speaker is reporting someone else's words without endorsing them.
questions.sourceLabel: Konjunktiv I & Reported Speech · Grammar drill

questions.prompt: Er sagte, er ___ keine Zeit.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I form of haben for er is habe: er habe keine Zeit.
questions.sourceLabel: Konjunktiv I & Reported Speech · Grammar drill

questions.prompt: Which noun comes from entscheiden?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ung forms die Entscheidung from the verb entscheiden.

questions.prompt: Das ___ (lesen) macht mir Freude.
questions.explanation: An infinitive used as a noun is neuter and capitalised: das Lesen.

questions.prompt: Which suffix forms a noun from frei?
questions.explanation: frei + -heit gives die Freiheit (freedom).

questions.prompt: Die ___ Kosten (steigen) beunruhigen uns.
questions.explanation: The present participle steigend takes the plural adjective ending -en: die steigenden Kosten.

questions.prompt: die betroffenen Personen means…
questions.explanation: The past participle betroffen is passive in meaning: the people who are affected.

questions.prompt: Die zu ___ Aufgaben (erledigen) sind im Anhang.
questions.explanation: zu + present participle + adjective ending: die zu erledigenden Aufgaben.

questions.prompt: Sobald means…
questions.explanation: sobald marks the point in time when something happens: as soon as.

questions.prompt: ___ die Ergebnisse vorliegen, informieren wir Sie.
questions.explanation: Sobald opens a subordinate clause and the verb vorliegen goes to the end.

questions.prompt: Which connector means “by doing so”?
questions.explanation: indem introduces the means by which something is achieved.

questions.prompt: Ich warte ___ eine Antwort.
questions.explanation: warten auf + accusative is a fixed combination: warten auf eine Antwort.

questions.prompt: Ich interessiere mich ___ Sprachen.
questions.explanation: sich interessieren für + accusative: sich für Sprachen interessieren.

questions.prompt: Worauf wartest du? refers to…
questions.explanation: wo- compounds refer to things. For people you would ask Auf wen wartest du?

questions.prompt: Das ist ___ interessant.
questions.explanation: ja signals shared knowledge or emphasis without changing the factual meaning.

questions.prompt: Es ist ___ nicht ganz einfach.
questions.explanation: halt expresses inevitability or resignation: it is just not that simple.

questions.prompt: Which particle can soften a request or add gentle contradiction?
questions.explanation: doch can soften a request (Komm doch mit) or gently contradict, depending on tone.

questions.prompt: Zwar ist die Maßnahme teuer, ___ ist sie langfristig wirtschaftlicher.
questions.explanation: jedoch fits the formal zwar … jedoch pattern and keeps the verb in position two.

questions.prompt: ___ es regnet, gehe ich spazieren.
questions.explanation: Obwohl introduces a concessive subordinate clause: although it is raining.

questions.prompt: Which is the most formal concession?
questions.explanation: wenngleich is formal or literary; obwohl and trotzdem are neutral.

questions.prompt: Which is appropriate in a formal email?
questions.explanation: Formal correspondence uses Sie and a complete, polite request.

questions.prompt: Formal German tends to use…
questions.explanation: Formal written German favours nominalisation, passive constructions and impersonal phrasing.

questions.prompt: Wir bitten ___ eine Rückmeldung.
questions.explanation: bitten um + accusative is the formal phrase: Wir bitten um eine Rückmeldung.

questions.prompt: Wir werden Ihren Vorschlag in Betracht ___.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is in Betracht ziehen: to take into consideration.

questions.prompt: zur Verfügung stellen means…
questions.explanation: zur Verfügung stellen = to make something available.

questions.prompt: Which is a function verb phrase?
questions.explanation: In eine Entscheidung treffen, the verb treffen carries little meaning; the noun carries the content.

questions.prompt: die von der Kommission beschlossene Reform means…
options: the reform that decided the commission
the reform passed by the commission
questions.explanation: beschlossene is a past participle attribute: the reform that was passed by the commission.

questions.prompt: die Bedeutung ___ Fortschritts
questions.explanation: Fortschritt is masculine, so the genitive article is des: die Bedeutung des Fortschritts.

questions.prompt: Genitive attributes usually come…
options: at the end of the sentence
questions.explanation: Genitive attributes follow the noun they describe: die Bedeutung des Fortschritts.

questions.prompt: Hätte man früher gehandelt, ___ das vermieden werden können.
questions.explanation: The counterfactual past uses hätte + past participle + modal infinitive: hätte vermieden werden können.

questions.prompt: Konjunktiv I primarily signals…
questions.explanation: Konjunktiv I marks reported speech and keeps the reporter neutral.

questions.prompt: Er sagte, er ___ gekommen, wenn er Zeit gehabt hätte.
questions.explanation: The unreal past conditional uses wäre gekommen: he would have come.

questions.prompt: Build: “This suggestion I consider problematic.”
questions.answer: Diesen Vorschlag halte ich für problematisch.
questions.explanation: Fronting the object creates focus, but the verb still occupies position two: Diesen Vorschlag halte ich …

questions.prompt: Fronting an object usually creates…
questions.explanation: Fronting moves emphasis to the element in position one.

questions.prompt: Nicht die Kosten sind das Problem, ___ die fehlende Zeit.
questions.explanation: nicht … sondern contrasts two alternatives: not the costs, but the lack of time.

questions.prompt: Austrian German for January is…
questions.explanation: Austrian German uses Jänner; Germany and most of Switzerland use Januar.

questions.prompt: Swiss German writes…
questions.explanation: Switzerland and Liechtenstein do not use ß; they write ss instead.

questions.prompt: Velo is Swiss German for…
questions.explanation: das Velo is the Swiss German word for bicycle.

questions.prompt: The default narrative tense in written fiction is…
questions.explanation: Written fiction normally narrates in the Präteritum; the Perfekt is more typical of speech.

questions.prompt: Sie ___ das Haus verlassen, bevor der Regen begann.
questions.explanation: The Plusquamperfekt marks the earlier action: sie hatte verlassen.

questions.prompt: Historical present creates…
questions.explanation: The historical present pulls the reader into the scene and creates immediacy.

questions.prompt: Which word is neutral for “cheap” in the sense of good value?
questions.explanation: günstig is neutral and positive. billig can sound dismissive; preiswert is also positive but more explicit.

questions.prompt: Which collocation is natural?
questions.explanation: German collocates Entscheidung with treffen: eine Entscheidung treffen.

questions.prompt: Die Entscheidung war schwierig, aber letztlich ___.
questions.explanation: tragfähig means sustainable or viable and fits a considered decision.

prompts.prompt: Introduce yourself and spell your first name letter by letter.

model.de: Guten Tag. Ich heiße Alex. A, L, E, X.
model.en: Good day. My name is Alex. A, L, E, X.

tips: Say the German letter names, not the English ones: Ah, Beh, Ceh, Deh …
If your name contains an umlaut, say the letter name and add “Umlaut”: Ü = “U-Umlaut”.
Record yourself, then compare your pace with the model. Clarity matters more than speed.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Introduce yourself and spell your first name letter by letter.

keyPhrase.de: Wie buchstabiert man das?
keyPhrase.en: How do you spell that?

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Wie buchstabiert man das?”.

prompts.prompt: Greet someone, give your name and say which country you come from. Add “Nice to meet you”.

model.de: Guten Tag! Ich heiße Sara. Ich komme aus Portugal. Freut mich, Sie kennenzulernen.
model.en: Good day! My name is Sara. I come from Portugal. Nice to meet you.

tips: Choose the register before you speak: Guten Tag + Sie for a stranger, Hallo + du for someone your age at a course.
Say Ich komme aus … as one block. Do not translate word by word from English “I am from”.
Record yourself and check the ending of the verb: kommst du, but kommen Sie.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Greet someone, give your name and say which country you come from. Add “Nice to meet you”.

keyPhrase.de: Freut mich, dich kennenzulernen.
keyPhrase.en: Nice to meet you.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Freut mich, dich kennenzulernen.”.

prompts.prompt: Give the date of your birthday, say which day your German course is on and what time it starts.

model.de: Mein Geburtstag ist am siebten April. Mein Deutschkurs ist am Montag. Er beginnt um halb sieben.
model.en: My birthday is on the seventh of April. My German course is on Monday. It begins at 6:30.

tips: Say the time twice: once with halb or Viertel, once with Uhr and minutes, so you hear the difference.
Keep the preposition with its noun: am Montag, im April, um sechs Uhr.
Record yourself and check that halb sieben came out as 6:30, not 7:30.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Give the date of your birthday, say which day your German course is on and what time it starts.

keyPhrase.de: Es ist halb drei.
keyPhrase.en: It is half past two (2:30).

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Es ist halb drei.”.

prompts.prompt: Say your name, your age, and what you have. Then describe one family member with sein.

model.de: Ich bin Mia. Ich bin zweiundzwanzig Jahre alt. Ich habe einen Bruder. Er ist Student.
model.en: I am Mia. I am twenty-two years old. I have a brother. He is a student.

tips: Use sein for who you are and how old you are; use haben only for things you possess.
Check the article of the noun before you choose einen, eine or ein.
Say the four sentences twice: the second time without looking at the model.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say your name, your age, and what you have. Then describe one family member with sein.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe einen Bruder.
keyPhrase.en: I have a brother.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich habe einen Bruder.”.

prompts.prompt: Say where you live, what you are learning and where you work or study. Use four sentences.

model.de: Ich wohne in Berlin. Ich lerne Deutsch. Ich arbeite in einem Büro. Am Abend spiele ich Tennis.
model.en: I live in Berlin. I am learning German. I work in an office. In the evening I play tennis.

tips: Say the verb and its ending together, as one word: wohn-e, wohn-st, wohn-t.
Start one sentence with a time phrase, such as Am Abend, and keep the verb in second position.
Record yourself and check that every sentence has exactly one conjugated verb.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say where you live, what you are learning and where you work or study. Use four sentences.

keyPhrase.de: Ich wohne in Berlin.
keyPhrase.en: I live in Berlin.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich wohne in Berlin.”.

prompts.prompt: Ask for a name, an origin and a reason for learning German. Then answer one of them yourself.

model.de: Wie heißt du? Woher kommst du? Warum lernst du Deutsch? — Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studiere.
model.en: What is your name? Where do you come from? Why are you learning German? — I am learning German because I study in Germany.

tips: Start each question with the question word and keep the verb directly after it.
For a yes/no question, begin with the verb and let your voice rise at the end.
Record the three questions, then listen for the difference between wo, wann and warum.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Ask for a name, an origin and a reason for learning German. Then answer one of them yourself.

keyPhrase.de: Sprichst du Englisch?
keyPhrase.en: Do you speak English?

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Sprichst du Englisch?”.

prompts.prompt: Say four sentences about your room. Name at least one masculine, one feminine and one neuter noun, plus one plural.

model.de: Das ist mein Zimmer. Der Tisch ist klein. Die Tür ist weiß. Das Fenster ist groß, und die Stühle sind alt.
model.en: This is my room. The table is small. The door is white. The window is big, and the chairs are old.

tips: Say the article and the noun as one unit, without a pause: derTisch, dieTür, dasFenster.
Check the plural article: it is always die, whatever the singular was.
Record yourself and listen for the umlauts in Tür, Stühle and Möbel.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say four sentences about your room. Name at least one masculine, one feminine and one neuter noun, plus one plural.

keyPhrase.de: Das ist ein Tisch.
keyPhrase.en: That is a table.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Das ist ein Tisch.”.

prompts.prompt: Say what you see in your room and what you need today. Use den or einen at least once.

model.de: Ich sehe den Tisch. Ich brauche einen neuen Stuhl.
model.en: I see the table. I need a new chair.

tips: Say the sentence once slowly, then once at normal speed.
Check that every masculine object has den or einen.
Use "Ich brauche …" to add a second sentence without extra grammar.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say what you see in your room and what you need today. Use den or einen at least once.

keyPhrase.de: Ich sehe den Hund.
keyPhrase.en: I see the dog.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich sehe den Hund.”.

prompts.prompt: Say two things you do not have and one thing that is yours.

model.de: Ich habe kein Auto. Ich habe keine Zeit. Das ist mein Fahrrad.
model.en: I have no car. I have no time. That is my bicycle.

tips: Use kein before the noun and check its gender.
Use nicht when you negate a verb: Ich arbeite nicht.
Say the three sentences without stopping, then listen to the model.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say two things you do not have and one thing that is yours.

keyPhrase.de: Das ist nicht mein Schlüssel.
keyPhrase.en: That is not my key.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Das ist nicht mein Schlüssel.”.

prompts.prompt: Introduce two family members and describe each one with one adjective.

model.de: Das ist meine Schwester. Sie ist sehr freundlich. Mein Bruder ist zehn Jahre alt.
model.en: This is my sister. She is very friendly. My brother is ten years old.

tips: Use meine before feminine nouns and mein before masculine or neuter nouns.
After ist, do not add an ending to the adjective.
Use "Das ist …" to introduce someone, then a second sentence to describe them.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Introduce two family members and describe each one with one adjective.

keyPhrase.de: Meine Schwester ist sehr freundlich.
keyPhrase.en: My sister is very friendly.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Meine Schwester ist sehr freundlich.”.

prompts.prompt: Order a drink and a snack, then ask for the price. Use hätte gern and Was kostet …?

model.de: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee und ein Brot. Was kostet das?
model.en: I would like a coffee and a bread. How much is that?

tips: Use einen for masculine drinks such as Kaffee and Tee.
Add "bitte" to sound polite without changing the grammar.
Say the price back to practise the numbers: drei Euro fünfzig.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Order a drink and a snack, then ask for the price. Use hätte gern and Was kostet …?

keyPhrase.de: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee, bitte.
keyPhrase.en: I would like a coffee, please.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee, bitte.”.

prompts.prompt: Describe your morning in three sentences. Use one separable verb and one time phrase.

model.de: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. Am Morgen trinke ich Kaffee. Dann kaufe ich ein.
model.en: I get up at seven. In the morning I drink coffee. Then I shop.

tips: Start with "Ich stehe … auf" and put the prefix at the end.
Use am for parts of the day and um for clock times.
Connect your sentences with dann or danach to sound more fluent.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe your morning in three sentences. Use one separable verb and one time phrase.

keyPhrase.de: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
keyPhrase.en: I get up at seven o'clock.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.”.

prompts.prompt: Describe your last weekend in four or five sentences. Use the Perfekt and at least one verb with sein.

model.de: Am Samstag habe ich lange geschlafen. Danach bin ich mit dem Fahrrad in die Stadt gefahren. Ich habe einen Freund getroffen, und wir haben zusammen zu Mittag gegessen. Am Abend bin ich zu Hause geblieben und habe einen Film gesehen. Am Sonntag habe ich meine Wohnung aufgeräumt.
model.en: On Saturday I slept late. Then I cycled into town. I met a friend, and we had lunch together. In the evening I stayed at home and watched a film. On Sunday I tidied my flat.

tips: Plan the auxiliary before you speak: say ich habe or ich bin, then finish the sentence with the participle.
Use the sein list deliberately: gehen, fahren, fliegen, kommen, bleiben, passieren.
Record yourself and listen for the final participle. If it is missing, the sentence sounds unfinished to a German ear.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe your last weekend in four or five sentences. Use the Perfekt and at least one verb with sein.

keyPhrase.de: Wir haben gestern einen Film gesehen.
keyPhrase.en: We watched a film yesterday.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Wir haben gestern einen Film gesehen.”.

prompts.prompt: Talk about your childhood or your first year at school in four sentences. Use war, hatte and at least one past modal.

model.de: Meine Kindheit war ziemlich ruhig. Wir hatten ein kleines Haus mit einem Garten. Ich konnte jeden Tag draußen spielen, aber ich musste abends um acht zu Hause sein. Damals war ich oft müde, aber sehr glücklich.
model.en: My childhood was quite quiet. We had a small house with a garden. I could play outside every day, but I had to be home at eight in the evening. Back then I was often tired, but very happy.

tips: Keep the modal's main verb in the infinitive at the end: ich musste … sein.
Use damals and als Kind to set the scene before your first verb.
Do not add an umlaut to konnte or musste — könnte and müsste mean something different.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Talk about your childhood or your first year at school in four sentences. Use war, hatte and at least one past modal.

keyPhrase.de: Als Kind war ich oft in den Bergen.
keyPhrase.en: As a child I was often in the mountains.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Als Kind war ich oft in den Bergen.”.

prompts.prompt: Tell a short travel story in five sentences. Use two time expressions and at least three sequencing words.

model.de: Letztes Jahr bin ich für eine Woche nach Wien gefahren. Zuerst habe ich mir das Zentrum angesehen. Danach bin ich in ein kleines Café gegangen und habe Kuchen gegessen. Am Abend habe ich einen Freund getroffen. Schließlich bin ich sehr müde ins Hotel zurückgegangen, aber es war ein toller Tag.
model.en: Last year I went to Vienna for a week. First I looked at the city centre. After that I went into a small café and ate cake. In the evening I met a friend. In the end I went back to the hotel very tired, but it was a great day.

tips: Say the time anchor before anything else, then put the verb immediately after it.
Use an die, in die or auf die for movement, and remember that these phrases come before the participle.
Do not use danach twice in a row. Vary with dann, anschließend and schließlich so the story keeps moving.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Tell a short travel story in five sentences. Use two time expressions and at least three sequencing words.

keyPhrase.de: Letztes Jahr bin ich nach Hamburg gereist.
keyPhrase.en: Last year I travelled to Hamburg.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Letztes Jahr bin ich nach Hamburg gereist.”.

prompts.prompt: Ask a stranger for help and thank them. Use at least three dative forms and one dative preposition.

model.de: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir bitte helfen? Ich suche den Bahnhof. Können Sie mir den Weg zeigen? Vielen Dank, das ist sehr freundlich von Ihnen. Ich danke Ihnen für die Hilfe.
model.en: Excuse me, can you help me, please? I am looking for the station. Can you show me the way? Many thanks, that is very kind of you. I thank you for your help.

tips: Use Ihnen with strangers and dir with friends. Mixing them sounds either rude or oddly intimate.
Keep the dative pronoun right after the verb: Können Sie mir helfen?
Remember that danken, helfen and gefallen never take mich, dich or ihn.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Ask a stranger for help and thank them. Use at least three dative forms and one dative preposition.

keyPhrase.de: Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
keyPhrase.en: Can you help me, please?

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Kannst du mir bitte helfen?”.

prompts.prompt: Say three sentences about a present you gave. Use at least two sentences with both a dative person and an accusative thing.

model.de: Meine Schwester hatte letzte Woche Geburtstag. Ich habe ihr ein Buch und eine Karte gekauft. Am Abend habe ich ihr das Geschenk gegeben, und sie hat sich sehr gefreut.
model.en: It was my sister's birthday last week. I bought her a book and a card. In the evening I gave her the present, and she was very happy.

tips: Keep the person before the thing when both are nouns: meiner Schwester ein Buch.
If you replace the thing with a pronoun, the pronoun comes first: Ich gebe es ihr.
Check the dative article before you speak. Saying ihrer Schwester instead of ihre Schwester is the whole difference between the cases.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say three sentences about a present you gave. Use at least two sentences with both a dative person and an accusative thing.

keyPhrase.de: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
keyPhrase.en: I give the child an apple.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.”.

prompts.prompt: Describe where four things are in your room, then say where you would move one of them. Use at least three two-way prepositions.

model.de: Mein Schreibtisch steht an der Wand, neben dem Fenster. Das Regal hängt über dem Schreibtisch. Meine Tasche liegt auf dem Boden unter dem Stuhl. Ich möchte das Regal an die andere Wand hängen, weil dort mehr Platz ist.
model.en: My desk is against the wall, next to the window. The shelf hangs above the desk. My bag is lying on the floor under the chair. I would like to hang the shelf on the other wall because there is more space there.

tips: Ask Wo? for the first three sentences and Wohin? for the change you describe.
Use the verb pairs: liegen/legen, stehen/stellen and hängen/hängen.
Listen to your article endings. dem signals a position, den signals a movement towards something.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe where four things are in your room, then say where you would move one of them. Use at least three two-way prepositions.

keyPhrase.de: Die Katze springt auf den Tisch.
keyPhrase.en: The cat jumps onto the table.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Die Katze springt auf den Tisch.”.

prompts.prompt: Say two things you must do this week and one thing you are allowed to do. Use modal verbs.

model.de: Ich muss am Montag arbeiten. Ich muss auch meine Eltern anrufen. Am Freitag darf ich früher nach Hause gehen.
model.en: I have to work on Monday. I also have to call my parents. On Friday I may go home earlier.

tips: Keep the modal in second position and the infinitive at the end.
Use darf for permission and muss for obligation.
Add a time phrase such as am Montag directly after the modal.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say two things you must do this week and one thing you are allowed to do. Use modal verbs.

keyPhrase.de: Ich muss heute länger arbeiten.
keyPhrase.en: I have to work longer today.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich muss heute länger arbeiten.”.

prompts.prompt: Say what you look forward to this week and what you do in the morning. Use one reflexive and one separable verb.

model.de: Ich freue mich auf Freitag. Ich stehe um sieben auf und rufe meine Mutter an.
model.en: I am looking forward to Friday. I get up at seven and call my mother.

tips: Use mich after ich and dich after du.
Put the separable prefix at the very end of the sentence.
Practise the pair as one chunk: ich freue mich auf …

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Say what you look forward to this week and what you do in the morning. Use one reflexive and one separable verb.

keyPhrase.de: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
keyPhrase.en: I am looking forward to the weekend.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.”.

prompts.prompt: Give a reason for learning German, a condition for practising, and a contrast about your schedule.

model.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland arbeiten möchte. Wenn ich Zeit habe, sehe ich deutsche Serien. Ich lerne auch am Wochenende, obwohl ich oft müde bin.
model.en: I am learning German because I want to work in Germany. When I have time, I watch German series. I also study at the weekend although I am often tired.

tips: Put the conjugated verb at the very end of each subordinate clause.
Use a comma before weil, dass, wenn and obwohl.
Start with wenn to vary your sentence rhythm.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Give a reason for learning German, a condition for practising, and a contrast about your schedule.

keyPhrase.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
keyPhrase.en: I am learning German because I want to study in Germany.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.”.

prompts.prompt: Compare two ways of travelling and say which is best for you.

model.de: Der Zug ist schneller als der Bus, aber der Bus ist günstiger. Für mich ist der Zug am besten, weil ich Zeit spare.
model.en: The train is faster than the bus, but the bus is cheaper. For me the train is best because I save time.

tips: Use -er plus als to compare two things.
Use am -sten for the best option.
Give a reason with weil to make your answer sound complete.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Compare two ways of travelling and say which is best for you.

keyPhrase.de: Der Zug ist schneller als der Bus.
keyPhrase.en: The train is faster than the bus.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Der Zug ist schneller als der Bus.”.

prompts.prompt: Describe your home or a place you know with three adjective + noun phrases.

model.de: Ich habe eine kleine Wohnung. Die helle Küche ist neu. Der große Balkon ist mein Lieblingsort.
model.en: I have a small flat. The bright kitchen is new. The large balcony is my favourite place.

tips: Use die + -e for feminine nouns and der + -e for masculine subjects.
Use den + -en when the masculine noun is a direct object.
Keep adjectives after sein ending-free.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe your home or a place you know with three adjective + noun phrases.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe den neuen Film gesehen.
keyPhrase.en: I saw the new film.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich habe den neuen Film gesehen.”.

prompts.prompt: Call a practice, describe one symptom and arrange an appointment for tomorrow.

model.de: Guten Tag, mein Name ist Anna Klein. Ich habe Schmerzen im Bein. Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren. Geht es morgen um zehn Uhr?
model.en: Hello, my name is Anna Klein. I have pain in my leg. I would like to make an appointment. Is tomorrow at ten possible?

tips: Open with your name and the reason for the call.
Use “Ich habe Schmerzen” or “Mir tut … weh”.
Ask for a specific time with “Geht es …?” to sound natural.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Call a practice, describe one symptom and arrange an appointment for tomorrow.

keyPhrase.de: Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren.
keyPhrase.en: I would like to make an appointment.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren.”.

prompts.prompt: Leave a short voicemail for a language school. Say who you are, ask politely for a call back and name a time when you are available.

model.de: Guten Tag, hier spricht Alex Weber. Ich hätte eine Frage zu meinem Kurs. Könnten Sie mich bitte zurückrufen? Ich wäre heute bis achtzehn Uhr erreichbar. Vielen Dank.
model.en: Good day, this is Alex Weber speaking. I have a question about my course. Could you call me back, please? I would be available today until six p.m. Thank you.

tips: Start with Guten Tag and your name; a voicemail without a name forces the listener to replay it.
Use one polite marker per request. Könnten Sie …? plus bitte is enough — do not stack three softeners.
End with a concrete time and Vielen Dank. That tells the office when to call and closes the message cleanly.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Leave a short voicemail for a language school. Say who you are, ask politely for a call back and name a time when you are available.

keyPhrase.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen?
keyPhrase.en: Could you help me, please?

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen?”.

prompts.prompt: Explain how you organise a busy week. Mention one problem, one consequence and one thing you do in addition.

model.de: In einer vollen Woche mache ich am Sonntag einen Plan, weil ich sonst zu viel vergesse. Montags habe ich meistens zwei Termine, deshalb stehe ich früher auf. Außerdem lasse ich abends das Handy im anderen Zimmer. Allerdings klappt das nicht immer.
model.en: In a busy week I make a plan on Sunday because otherwise I forget too much. On Mondays I usually have two appointments, so I get up earlier. I also leave my phone in another room in the evening. However, that does not always work.

tips: Plan your verb position before you speak: deshalb + verb + subject, weil + subject + verb.
Use one clear example per connector. Three well-linked sentences beat six short, unconnected ones.
Stress the connector slightly so the listener can follow the logic of your answer.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Explain how you organise a busy week. Mention one problem, one consequence and one thing you do in addition.

keyPhrase.de: Es regnet, trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.
keyPhrase.en: It is raining; nevertheless, I am going for a walk.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Es regnet, trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.”.

prompts.prompt: Should students work part-time while studying? Give your opinion, support it with one reason and one example, and acknowledge the other side.

model.de: Meiner Meinung nach ist ein Nebenjob während des Studiums sinnvoll, weil man praktische Erfahrung sammelt. Ein Beispiel dafür ist mein Freund, der durch seinen Job im Café besser Deutsch gelernt hat. Natürlich stimmt es, dass zu viel Arbeit das Studium belastet. Deshalb finde ich, dass zehn Stunden pro Woche genug sind.
model.en: In my opinion, a part-time job during university is sensible because you gain practical experience. One example is my friend, who learned German better through his job in a café. Of course it is true that too much work puts pressure on your studies. That is why I think ten hours a week are enough.

tips: Start with one clear frame — Meiner Meinung nach or Ich finde, dass — and do not stack several openers.
Give a real or realistic example after your reason; it makes the opinion sound grounded.
Add one concession with Natürlich stimmt es, dass … and then return to your position.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Should students work part-time while studying? Give your opinion, support it with one reason and one example, and acknowledge the other side.

keyPhrase.de: Meiner Meinung nach sollte man mehr Rad fahren.
keyPhrase.en: In my opinion, people should cycle more.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Meiner Meinung nach sollte man mehr Rad fahren.”.

prompts.prompt: Describe a person you work or study with, a place you like and an object you use every day. Use a relative clause for each one.

model.de: Eine Kollegin, die ich sehr schätze, arbeitet seit fünf Jahren bei uns. Wir treffen uns oft in dem Café, das direkt gegenüber liegt. Dort benutze ich immer das alte Notizbuch, das mir mein Vater geschenkt hat.
model.en: A colleague whom I value highly has worked with us for five years. We often meet in the café that is directly opposite. There I always use the old notebook that my father gave me.

tips: Say the noun first, then decide gender and number, then choose the case from the role in the clause.
Keep each relative clause short in speech. One clear clause is better than three nested ones.
Use a preposition with a place: das Café, in dem … or das Büro, in dem … — it sounds more precise than wo in a prepared answer.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe a person you work or study with, a place you like and an object you use every day. Use a relative clause for each one.

keyPhrase.de: Das ist der Kollege, der mir geholfen hat.
keyPhrase.en: That is the colleague who helped me.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Das ist der Kollege, der mir geholfen hat.”.

prompts.prompt: Talk about your plans for next year. Mention one thing you intend to do, one thing you are trying to improve and one purpose behind your plan.

model.de: Ich habe vor, nächstes Jahr einen Sprachkurs in Deutschland zu machen. Ich versuche, vorher jeden Tag zwanzig Minuten zu üben, um sicherer zu sprechen. Außerdem habe ich vor, mich für eine Prüfung anzumelden. Ich hoffe, sie im Sommer zu bestehen.
model.en: I plan to take a language course in Germany next year. I am trying to practise twenty minutes every day beforehand in order to speak more confidently. I also plan to register for an exam. I hope to pass it in the summer.

tips: Keep the zu-infinitive at the end of its clause; do not insert the object after it.
Use um … zu only when you are the person doing both actions. Otherwise switch to damit.
Build one sentence at a time. A clear plan plus a clear purpose is enough for a strong B1 answer.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Talk about your plans for next year. Mention one thing you intend to do, one thing you are trying to improve and one purpose behind your plan.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe vor, im Sommer nach Wien zu fahren.
keyPhrase.en: I plan to go to Vienna in the summer.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich habe vor, im Sommer nach Wien zu fahren.”.

prompts.prompt: Talk about your hobbies and interests. Say what you are interested in, what you are looking forward to and what you are currently working on.

model.de: Ich interessiere mich für Musik und Fotografie. Im Moment beschäftige ich mich mit einem kleinen Fotoprojekt über meine Stadt. Ich freue mich schon auf den Sommer, weil ich dann mehr Zeit dafür habe. Außerdem denke ich oft an meine Familie, die weit weg wohnt.
model.en: I am interested in music and photography. At the moment I am working on a small photo project about my city. I am already looking forward to the summer, because I will have more time for it then. I also often think of my family, who live far away.

tips: Say the pair as one block — interessiere mich für — instead of translating the preposition from English.
Check the case after the preposition: für + accusative, mit + dative, von + dative.
Use a da-compound to avoid repeating a long noun: Ich freue mich darauf, statt Ich freue mich auf das Projekt.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Talk about your hobbies and interests. Say what you are interested in, what you are looking forward to and what you are currently working on.

keyPhrase.de: Ich interessiere mich für deutsche Geschichte.
keyPhrase.en: I am interested in German history.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Ich interessiere mich für deutsche Geschichte.”.

prompts.prompt: Introduce yourself formally on the phone, state your request and close politely.

model.de: Guten Tag, mein Name ist Ali Yildiz. Ich rufe wegen meines Termins an. Könnten Sie mir bitte einen neuen Termin geben? Vielen Dank. Auf Wiederhören.
model.en: Hello, my name is Ali Yildiz. I am calling about my appointment. Could you please give me a new appointment? Thank you. Goodbye.

tips: Use Sie and your full name in formal calls.
State the reason with “Ich rufe wegen … an”.
Close with “Vielen Dank. Auf Wiederhören.”

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Introduce yourself formally on the phone, state your request and close politely.

keyPhrase.de: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,
keyPhrase.en: Dear Sir or Madam,

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,”.

prompts.prompt: Draft and say a short formal email: subject, greeting, reason, request and closing.

model.de: Betreff: Frage zu meinem Kurs. Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, ich schreibe Ihnen wegen meines Kurses. Könnten Sie mir bitte den neuen Termin mitteilen? Vielen Dank. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ali Yildiz.
model.en: Subject: Question about my course. Dear Ms Weber, I am writing to you about my course. Could you please let me know the new date? Thank you. Kind regards, Ali Yildiz.

tips: Say the subject line first, as if you were reading the email aloud.
Keep the request to one sentence.
Use the same formal closing every time so it becomes automatic.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Draft and say a short formal email: subject, greeting, reason, request and closing.

keyPhrase.de: Mit freundlichen Grüßen
keyPhrase.en: Kind regards

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
Capitalise every German noun.
Check that the verb agrees with its subject.
Try to use: “Mit freundlichen Grüßen”.

prompts.prompt: Describe three things that happen in your town without saying who does them. Use the passive.

model.de: Jeden Samstag wird der Markt geöffnet. Die Straßen werden am Morgen gereinigt. Im Sommer werden viele Feste gefeiert.
model.en: Every Saturday the market is opened. The streets are cleaned in the morning. In summer many festivals are celebrated.

tips: Start with the thing affected, then use werden + participle.
Keep the participle at the end of the clause.
Use wurde for a completed past event.

prompts.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences in German. Describe three things that happen in your town without saying who does them. Use the passive.

keyPhrase.de: Die Rechnung wird morgen bezahlt.
keyPhrase.en: The invoice will be paid tomorrow.

checklist: Start each sentence with a capital letter.
